name: Wire-Tech
old_description: Wire Tech has been making components for handgun and rifles since 1996. What constitutes a good firearm? We agree with most owners who say a firearm that is manufactured with quality workmanship would produce the one needed ingredient: reliability. This is something that WireTech strides to achieve with every job, customer and commitment.
about:
Wire Tech LLC operates from Watertown, Connecticut, where it has been producing precision components since 1996. The company began by making parts for handguns and rifles, establishing a reputation for reliability in small-arms manufacturing.

The shop specializes in wire EDM, sinker EDM, and fast-hole drilling, supported by CNC milling, grinding, and heat-treating in a fully equipped tool room. Its machine lineup includes multiple Mitsubishi wire EDMs (FX10, FA-V, FX20K, FX-10K, FA-10V), a Sodick ALN600G and MV1200R, a CNC Ct300 fast-hole driller, and an EX-8 sinker EDM. Work ranges from single prototypes to full production runs, with programming handled by experienced tool and die makers using ESPRIT CAM software.

Wire Tech serves the medical, firearms, aerospace, automotive, aircraft, electronics, instrumentation, and molding industries. Customers include manufacturers of surgical instruments, firearm components, aerospace fixtures, and progressive stamping dies. The company also builds assembly tools, test fixtures, and welding fixtures for these sectors.

The company emphasizes that its programming and setups are performed by diemakers who understand part function and clearances, allowing computerized monitoring to catch deviations early. It offers 24-hour emergency service, retains all job data for exact repeat orders, and holds ISO 9001:2015 certification.

name: Wisconsin Metal Parts
old_description: Since 1988, we have provided high-quality manufacturing solutions for companies across the country
about:
Wisconsin Metal Parts operates from Waukesha, Wisconsin. The company was founded in 1988 as Die Concepts, Inc., and spent its first 22 years building a tool-and-die business while listening to customer needs. In 2010 it rebranded to Wisconsin Metal Parts to reflect a broader service portfolio, and in 2024 it was acquired by SOLV Metals to join a larger group of metal manufacturers. Ownership and management have remained consistent through the transitions.

The shop provides full-service metal manufacturing under one roof, including CNC machining (turning, milling, drilling, tapping, boring, grinding), sheet metal fabrication (fiber laser cutting, CNC punching, bending, forming, welding, hardware insertion), custom metal stamping (progressive die, prototype to production), wire EDM (up to 16″ thick in conductive materials, including carbide), and tool-and-die design and build using simulation software. It runs nearly 60 million stampings per year at a 98% on-time delivery rate from two facilities in the Waukesha area.

Customers span aerospace, agriculture, foodservice, medical, and defense sectors. The company has produced military ordnance components such as mechanical fuzes, high-volume progressive die stampings for the container industry, and assemblies ranging from cabinets to clamping fixtures. It also supports commercial and industrial clients nationwide.

Wisconsin Metal Parts emphasizes intellectual value and a “Golden Rule” culture—treating customers, employees, and suppliers with respect. Its cross-trained workforce moves between departments to maintain workflow, and in-house tooling capabilities allow it to take over existing stamping dies and manage complex, multi-process parts from prototype through assembly.

We handle everything from large modular and  construction projects all the way down to small repair work and support members for residential projects. We are a family business run by two brothers born and raised in Berlin WI. Since our inception in a small 900 sq ft, back yard garage with just a few welders, and a small forklift, we have proven that no job is too big or too small for us to be able to tackle. We now have grown to a 12 acre, 25,000 square ft facility with cutting edge equipment and experienced staff. We pride ourselves on Quality and on time delivery. about:
Wisconsin Steel Fabrication LLC operates from Omro, Wisconsin. Founded by two brothers raised in nearby Berlin, the company began in a 900-square-foot backyard garage equipped with a few welders and a small forklift. It remains a family-owned business.

The shop provides steel fabrication and manufacturing services including large modular fabrication, small modular fabrication, structural steel, custom fabrication, railings and stairs, and certified welding. From its original garage, the operation has expanded to a 12-acre campus with a 25,000-square-foot facility housing modern equipment and an experienced staff.

The company serves construction and modular building sectors, handling projects that range from large-scale modular and commercial construction down to small repair jobs and residential support members. Customers include general contractors, modular builders, and homeowners needing custom steel components.

Leadership emphasizes quality and on-time delivery as core differentiators, stating that customer satisfaction drives the business. The team promotes a willingness to tackle any project regardless of size, aiming to turn client ideas into finished fabrications.

name: Wisconsin Wire Works, Inc.
old_description: Wisconsin Wire Works Inc. is an integrated manufacturer of copper and copper alloy welding wire. Five copper-industry veterans founded our company in 1994, and in a relatively short time, we've built an enviable reputation as a reliable supplier of top-quality, made-in-the-USA welding products. Today, our customers can be found on every continent.
about:
Wisconsin Wire Works, Inc. operates from Wales, Wisconsin, where five copper-industry veterans founded the company in 1994. The business remains under the leadership of the founding family: John Turriff serves as president and owner, with Tressa Turriff and Ryan Turriff as vice presidents, and Jeremy Hoadley as sales manager.

The company manufactures copper and copper alloy welding wire, including aluminum bronze, silicon bronze, deoxidized copper, phosphor bronze, nickel aluminum bronze, and copper alloy brazing wires. Production centers on state-of-the-art drawing equipment maintained on a scheduled die-rework program, with a thorough inspection program that checks size, cleanliness, cast, and helix before any product ships. An in-house welding facility and a staff of welding engineers, metallurgists, and fabrication specialists provide technical support and product testing.

Customers span welders, fabricators, and manufacturers on every continent. The wire is supplied in precision layer-level wound spools, straightened-and-cut lengths, reels, coils, and barrel packs, all packaged in robust cartons with hermetic moisture barriers for long shelf life and secure international shipment.

The founders built the company on listening to customers — staying small enough to know them well and surveying them regularly. That approach, combined with a commitment to made-in-the-USA quality, non-contaminating lubricants, minimal landfill waste, and thorough cleaning before shipment, is what the company says sets it apart.

name: Wise Plastics
old_description: 100+ presses from 35 to 1100 tons, liquid silicone molding, and value-added operations under one quality system — 30 minutes from Chicago and O'Hare.
about:
Wise Plastics Technologies traces its roots to 1974, when it was founded as Wise‑Hamlin Plastics in the greater Chicagoland area. Today the company is headquartered in St. Charles, Illinois, with additional facilities in West Chicago, placing it roughly 30 minutes from downtown Chicago and O’Hare International Airport.

The molder operates more than 100 injection presses ranging from 35 to 1,100 tons across three purpose‑built plants totaling over 350,000 square feet. Core processes include precision plastic injection molding, two‑shot, insert and over‑molding, liquid silicone rubber (LSR) molding for medical‑grade and biocompatible applications, and scientific molding supported by RJG‑certified decoupled processes and automation on every cell. Value‑added services span assembly, sonic welding, heat staking, decorating, packaging, kitting, and full contract‑manufacturing programs that cover tooling transfers, design‑for‑manufacturing, supply‑chain management, and just‑in‑time delivery. A staff of 200+ runs production 24/5, shifting to 24/7 when demand requires.

The company serves medical device and pharmaceutical customers with ISO 13485:2016‑certified quality systems and clean‑room LSR capability, defense programs under ITAR registration, and a broad range of industrial OEMs that rely on its integrated supply‑chain and logistics support.

Wise Plastics emphasizes five decades of manufacturing discipline, modern equipment, and a quality‑first culture codified in ISO 9001:2015 and OSHA SHARP certifications. Its stated differentiators include purpose‑built facilities, integrated operations, advanced automation, an experienced team, ultra‑responsive service, and a commitment to continuous improvement across quality, innovation, employee respect, integrity, and sustainability.

name: WishBone Medical, Inc.
old_description: WishBone Medical is a Warsaw, IN, based pediatric orthopedic company focused globally on the unmet needs of children suffering from orthopedic issues. Our mission is to provide anatomically appropriate solutions in single-use, sterile packed procedure kits to surgeons and their patients who are still growing.
about:
WishBone Medical operates from Warsaw, Indiana, the heart of the orthopedic manufacturing corridor. The company was established to address unmet needs in pediatric orthopedics, focusing on children who are still growing.

The company designs and supplies anatomically appropriate implants and instruments packaged as single-use, sterile procedure kits. Its product lines include growth control systems, plating systems, and bone void fillers, all delivered in multi-barrier sterile packaging. Instruments such as screwdrivers and depth gauges are included in each kit, eliminating the need for reusable trays and loaner sets.

WishBone Medical serves pediatric orthopedic surgeons, hospitals, and surgical centers. Its kits are used in procedures for children with orthopedic conditions, providing a sterile, ready-to-use alternative to traditional reusable instrument sets.

The company emphasizes that its single-use model reduces infection risk, cuts operating room turnover time by eliminating set reprocessing, and avoids the logistical burden of loaner trays. Every instrument is new and sharp for each procedure, and kits are stocked for immediate availability.

name: Wolf Metals
old_description: Wolf Metals has been at the forefront of custom metal fabrication in Ohio for over three decades. Founded in 1974 by Jim and Mike Wolf, our family-owned company has grown from a small local shop to a leading metal fabrication expert serving industries across the United States.
about:
Wolf Metals operates from Columbus, Ohio, where it was founded in 1974 by Jim and Mike Wolf as a family-owned metal fabrication shop. Over three decades, the company has grown from a small local operation into a full-service fabrication specialist serving customers across the United States.

The company provides a broad range of metal fabrication processes under one roof, including laser cutting, water jet cutting, forming (bending, rolling, stamping), shearing, MIG and TIG welding, fastener insertion, powder coating, plating, assembly, CNC machining, leveling, tube laser cutting, laser welding, and aluminum composite material (ACM) fabrication. Its 100,000-square-foot facility houses more than 50 state-of-the-art machines, such as CNC machining centers, robotic welding cells, laser cutting systems, and a fully automated robotic bend cell. Wolf Metals handles projects from one-off prototypes to large production runs.

The shop serves industries including automotive, aerospace, defense, energy, medical, agriculture, construction, and industrial machinery. A recent project involved engineering a modular aluminum exoskeleton for DTi Creative, enabling marching bands to transform a John Deere Gator into performance vehicles such as a lunar rover and a pirate ship.

Wolf Metals emphasizes uncompromising quality, continuous innovation, customer focus, integrity, and teamwork as core values. The company cites a 99.8% on-time delivery rate and a defect rate below 0.1% as measurable outcomes of its approach, and highlights its centrally located Ohio facility for efficient nationwide service.

old_description: Wolfe Custom Woodworking LLC is a full service design, fabrication and installation shop serving the Denver Metro Area. We focus primarily on creating built-in cabinetry, shelving, and stand alone hardwood tables and casework.
about:
Wolfe Custom Woodworking LLC operates from Englewood, Colorado, serving the Denver metropolitan area. The company was founded by Daniel E. Wolfe, who has spent many years crafting fine furniture and cabinets before establishing the business as a full-service design, fabrication, and installation shop.

The shop specializes in built-in cabinetry, custom shelving, and stand-alone hardwood tables and casework. Every project moves through design, fabrication, and installation, with all work performed by Wolfe himself. Recent projects include a white oak banquette and dining table, a walnut banquette, a mid-century modern media credenza, a solid walnut bookshelf, a shaker hutch, and a modern side table featuring a bookmatched Indian rosewood top with bowtie joints and hand-carved bevel.

The client base is primarily residential customers in the Denver Metro Area seeking custom woodwork for kitchens, dining rooms, living rooms, and home offices. The portfolio also shows vinyl casework, indicating some commercial or specialty work.

Wolfe emphasizes a hands-on approach: each piece is designed and fabricated with his own two hands, and he encourages clients to participate in the design process so the final product reflects their exact vision. This personal involvement and focus on long-lasting quality are presented as the core reasons the business exists.
